# GEO report: harbor-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 40/100, At risk

Confidence: High (checked 25 of 25 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16.33 ÷ 25 × 100 = 65. High = (16.33 + 0) ÷ 25 × 100 = 65. Both are capped at 40, because `robots.txt` blocks a search crawler from the whole site (GEO-009).

All of this was read from code. The site is an Astro site with three pages, and the uncapped result would be a reasonable 65. The cap applies because two AI search crawlers are told to stay out completely. Nothing was left unknown.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Let the AI search crawlers in (or confirm that you meant to block them)
- **Why it matters:** `OAI-SearchBot` (ChatGPT search) and `PerplexityBot` are crawlers that power AI search answers. Blocking them site-wide keeps the site out of those tools. I assumed you want to be found, because there is no `geo.config.json`.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4-8`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: OAI-SearchBot` / `Disallow: /` and `User-agent: PerplexityBot` / `Disallow: /`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 77/100 on its own, because the cap of 40 is lifted.

### 2. Repair the two broken structured data blocks
- **Why it matters:** JSON-LD is a label that tells machines what a page is. Broken labels get ignored.
- **Where:**
  - `src/data/faq.json:8`: the key is blank. Rename `" "` to `"acceptedAnswer"`.
  - `src/pages/moorings.astro:9`: remove the trailing comma, which makes the JSON invalid.
- **What the code says:** `" ": {` and `"headline": "Moorings and prices", }`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 73 without the cap. It stays at 40 until item 1 is done. With items 1 and 2 together it is 85.

### 3. Give each page its own canonical URL
- **Why it matters:** a canonical link says "this is the main address of this page". Yours says the home page for every page, so search engines are told `/moorings` and `/contact` are duplicates of `/`.
- **Where:** `src/layouts/Base.astro:8`
- **What the code says:** `<link rel="canonical" href="https://harbor.example/" />`
- **Size:** Small. Build the URL from `Astro.url.pathname` and a `site` setting in the Astro config.
- **Score after this:** 71 without the cap, still 40 until item 1 is done. With all three items it is 91.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt valid and reachable | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt` is plain text and valid |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access you intend | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:4-8`, site-wide, 0 of 3 routes |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | Not run | `src/pages/contact.astro:4` has `robots="noindex"` but is in the sitemap and nav (2 of 3 routes clear) |

| GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Clear | Not run | Astro renders on the server, and the `client:load` form is also server-rendered |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD valid | Problem | Not run | `src/data/faq.json:8` and `src/pages/moorings.astro:9`, 0 of 2 routes with JSON-LD clear |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap discoverable | Clear | Not run | `public/sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt:10` |
| GEO-012 | Title, description, lang | Clear | Not run | `src/layouts/Base.astro:4-7`, set on all 3 routes |

| GEO-017 | No snippet blocking | Problem | Not run | `src/layouts/Base.astro:9`, `max-snippet:0` by default on `/` and `/moorings` (1 of 3 clear) |

| GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared |

## Other problems found

None found beyond the results above.

## Worth considering

- **FAQ markup with no visible FAQ:** `src/pages/index.astro:8`: `JSON.stringify(faq)`. The page labels two questions (night booking, water taxi) that it never shows. Showing them as text would let readers and machines see the same facts.
- **Contact details label:** `src/pages/contact.astro:6`: `Call the harbour office on 01326 000000.` This page is marked noindex, so the office phone number is hidden from search. If that isn't deliberate, drop the noindex and consider `LocalBusiness` structured data with the address and phone number.
- **Prices as structured data:** `src/pages/moorings.astro:7`: `Prices start at £40 a night.` The page is labelled as an `Article`. An offer or price label might describe it better.
- **Head basics:** `src/layouts/Base.astro:5-10` has no `charset` or `viewport` meta tag and no `<main>` around the `<slot />`.
- **Blocked crawlers:** if blocking `PerplexityBot` was deliberate, note that `GPTBot` and `ClaudeBot` (training crawlers) are not mentioned in `public/robots.txt`. A stated policy should apply to all of them.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **`llms.txt` (info only):** none present, which is fine.

## Assumptions

- You want search and AI search tools to find this site. There is no `geo.config.json`.
- `https://harbor.example` is the intended domain, taken from `robots.txt` and the sitemap.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-009`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
